executive_summary: The customer's accounts payable team of three people processes between 4,500 and 5,200 invoices per month. Today, invoices arrive by email, are keyed into NetSuite manually, and matched against the purchase order and goods receipt. Clean invoices take about two days; exceptions involving price differences or missing receipts take closer to five days and keep the team late at month end, especially after new suppliers were onboarded in September.

The customers have stated two explicit goals: automatic matching of clean invoices with a short list of real exceptions for the team to review, and a clear record of who approved what. They also raised supplier onboarding as a follow-on priority if the invoice work goes well. Today, about 60 open exceptions are tracked in a single person's spreadsheet updated by hand every morning, and the approval trail had to be rebuilt from emails when auditors asked.

Several unconfirmed hypotheses emerged: the solution may need to capture and extract invoice data from the ap-invoices mailbox before matching can be automated; a read-only NetSuite integration might deliver early value without waiting for a security review; the weekly-only supplier portal CSV feed may conflict with the proposed daily exceptions list; and email is acting as the de facto workflow for exceptions and approvals. Nobody has measured the volume or causes of exceptions, which would set a baseline for success.

The biggest blockers are that write access to NetSuite requires a security review taking a few weeks to schedule, the supplier portal has no API and only provides a weekly CSV export, and the exceptions spreadsheet owner is reluctant to share it outside finance until the customer's lead approves. The previous RPA approach failed because it relied on screen layout, which may make the customers wary of brittle automation.

use_case_summaries.UC-1: Automatic matching of clean invoices with a daily exceptions list that replaces the hand-updated spreadsheet. Matches invoices against purchase orders and goods receipts; unmatched items go to a short list for manual review.
use_case_summaries.UC-2: A read-only integration to NetSuite that avoids the security review delay, allowing matching analysis to begin while write-access approvals are scheduled. Results would be returned to NetSuite by user import or an existing feed rather than direct tool write.
use_case_summaries.UC-3: Automated capture and extraction of invoice data from the ap-invoices shared mailbox, removing manual keying for a volume that has grown to 5,200 invoices in busy months on a three-person team.
use_case_summaries.UC-4: A robust pipeline to ingest the weekly supplier portal CSV export that does not break when the portal layout changes, and a clarification of whether daily exceptions can be supported when portal data arrives only once per week.
use_case_summaries.UC-5: Baseline measurement and analytics of exceptions by count, age, cause, supplier, and month. Nobody has measured how many exceptions occur or why, so success cannot be shown and root causes cannot be addressed.
use_case_summaries.UC-6: Automated approval routing and audit trail. Approvals are currently a record in emails and had to be rebuilt for auditors. Approval thresholds differ by supplier category and are kept in a SharePoint document that is not always current.
use_case_summaries.UC-7: Shared supplier master data linking invoice approval routing to onboarding, so that supplier categories recorded during onboarding automatically set approval thresholds and stay current.
use_case_summaries.UC-8: Automated exception and approval workflow to replace email chasing. When Raj is unavailable, people are contacted by email; this defines email as the workflow and record system for both exceptions and approvals.
use_case_summaries.UC-9: Capacity planning for supplier growth. Invoice volume grew after new suppliers were onboarded in September while team size remained at three people. The solution must scale and onboarding speed affects AP volume.
use_case_summaries.UC-10: Faster supplier onboarding. The customer stated that onboarding takes far too long and would like to tackle it next if invoice automation goes well. The current onboarding process and timeline were not described.
use_case_summaries.UC-11: Finance data access governance. The exceptions spreadsheet owner is reluctant to share exception data outside finance, implying the new solution will need role-based access controls and data handling rules for sensitive financial data.

opportunity_narratives.UC-2: A read-only integration could deliver value without waiting for the NetSuite security review, which takes a few weeks to schedule. If matched invoice results can be returned to NetSuite through a user import or existing feed rather than direct tool write access, the engagement can start sooner and de-risk the delivery schedule.
opportunity_narratives.UC-3: Automatic invoice capture and data extraction from the ap-invoices mailbox is prerequisite to any automatic matching. The team processes 5,200 invoices per month and someone opens each one to key it into NetSuite by hand, so automating intake removes the bottleneck and scales with new suppliers without adding headcount.
opportunity_narratives.UC-4: The solution is proposed to deliver a daily exceptions list, but the only supplier portal data feed is a weekly CSV. Resolving this data freshness conflict early—either by running exports more often, using alternative data sources for goods receipts, or resetting expectations on the exceptions cadence—prevents a repeat of the earlier RPA failure and sets realistic timelines.
opportunity_narratives.UC-5: No one has measured exception volume, trends, or causes despite them taking five days and keeping the team late at month end. Establishing a baseline count and analytics on price differences, missing receipts, and other root causes allows the team to target the most common problems and gives measurable proof that the solution works.
opportunity_narratives.UC-7: Approval thresholds are out of date in a SharePoint document and differ by supplier category. Linking supplier master data from onboarding to invoice routing keeps thresholds current and avoids rework during the follow-on onboarding engagement, making the two projects cohesive.
